arxiv-2204-09126.title: Measuring the Soft X-Ray Quantum Efficiency of a Hybrid CMOS Detector
arxiv-2204-09126.creator: Joseph M. Colosimo, Abraham D. Falcone, Mitchell Wages, Samuel V. Hull, Daniel M. LaRocca, David N. Burrows, Cole R. Armstrong, Gooderham McCormick, Mitchell Range, Fredric Hancock
arxiv-2204-09126.description: Abstract Next-generation X-ray observatories, such as the Lynx X-ray Observatory Mission Concept or other similar concepts in the coming decade, will require detectors with high quantum efficiency (QE) across the soft X-ray band to observe the faint objects that drive their mission science objectives.

arxiv-2212-05736.title: Stability analysis of mean field type control system with major agent
arxiv-2212-05736.creator: Yurii Averboukh
arxiv-2212-05736.description: Abstract The paper is concerned with the study of a control system consisting of one major agent and many identical minor agents in the limit case when the number of agents tends to infinity. To study the limiting system we use the mean field approach.

arxiv-2302-07422.title: Entropy and stability of hyperbolic manifolds
arxiv-2302-07422.creator: Antoine Song
arxiv-2302-07422.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Antoine Song. Let ( M , g 0 ) (M,g_{0}) be a closed oriented hyperbolic manifold of dimension at least 3 3 . By the volume entropy inequality of G. Gallot, for any Riemannian metric g g on M M with same volume as g 0 g_{0} , its volume entropy h ⁡ ( g ) h(g) satisfies h ⁡ ( g ) ≥ n − 1 h(g)\geq n-1 with equality only when g g is isometric to g 0 g_{0} .

arxiv-2401-02506.title: Student gender modulates the intersection of calculus proficiency and calculus self-efficacy in an introductory electricity and magnetism course
arxiv-2401-02506.creator: Christopher J. Fischer
arxiv-2401-02506.description: Abstract Abstract We assessed changes in calculus proficiency and calculus self-efficacy in a second semester course of introductory physics focused on electricity and magnetism. While all students demonstrated an increase in calculus proficiency, including a possible improvement in calculus transfer to physics, women displayed larger gains than men. Conversely, men showed larger gains in calculus self-efficacy.

arxiv-2406-02022.title: Density functional Bogoliubov-de Gennes theory for superconductors implemented in the SIESTA code
arxiv-2406-02022.creator: R. Reho 1 , N. Wittemeier 2 , A. H. Kole 1 , P. Ordejón 2 , Z. Zanolli
arxiv-2406-02022.description: Abstract We present SIESTA -BdG, an implementation of the simultaneous solution of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) and Density Functional Theory (DFT) problem in SIESTA , a first-principles method and code for material simulations which uses pseudopotentials and a localized basis set. This unified approach describes both conventional and unconventional superconducting states, and enables a description of inhomogeneous superconductors and heterostructures.

arxiv-2412-07084.title: Atomic number estimation of dual energy cargo radiographs: initial experimental results using a semiempirical transparency model
arxiv-2412-07084.creator: Peter Lalor, Areg Danagoulian
arxiv-2412-07084.description: Abstract To combat the risk of nuclear smuggling, radiography systems are deployed at ports to scan cargo containers for concealed illicit materials. Dual energy radiography systems enable a rough elemental analysis of cargo containers due to the Z-dependence of photon attenuation, allowing for improved material detection.

arxiv-2508-17665.title: Testing the weak cosmic censorship conjecture via test particle-induced overcharging/overspinning of Kerr–Newman-modified gravity black hole
arxiv-2508-17665.creator: Waqar Ahmad (waqar.ahmad@cust.edu.pk), Abdul Rehman Kashif (kashmology@gmail.com)
arxiv-2508-17665.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Waqar Ahmad (waqar.ahmad@cust.edu.pk), Abdul Rehman Kashif (kashmology@gmail.com). We investigate the weak cosmic censorship conjecture (WCCC) violation through the absorption of a charged, rotating test particle by Kerr-Newman spacetime in modified gravity (KN-MOG). The result is sensitive to multiple factors, including the sign of the particle’s charge relative to that of the black hole, as well as the direction of rotation of the particle and the black hole.

arxiv-2601-07950.title: The Davenport constant of an interval: a proof that 𝖣 = χ {\mathsf{D}=\chi}
arxiv-2601-07950.creator: Benjamin Girard, Alain Plagne
arxiv-2601-07950.description: Abstract . For two positive integers m m and M M , we study the Davenport constant of the interval of integers ⟦ − m , M ⟧ \llbracket-m,M\rrbracket , that is the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence composed of elements from ⟦ − m , M ⟧ \llbracket-m,M\rrbracket .

arxiv-2602-17835.title: Influence-Preserving Proxies for Gradient-Based Data Selection in LLM Fine-tuning
arxiv-2602-17835.creator: Sirui Chen, Yunzhe Qi, Mengting Ai, Yifan Sun, Ruizhong Qiu, Jiaru Zou, Jingrui HeUniversity of Illinois Urbana-Champaign {sirui6, yunzheq2, mai10, yifan50, rq5, jiaruz2, jingrui}@illinois.edu
arxiv-2602-17835.description: Abstract Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) relies critically on selecting training data that most benefits model’s downstream performance. Gradient-based data selection methods such as TracIn and Influence Functions leverage influence to identify useful samples, but their computational cost scales poorly, making them impractical for multi-billion-parameter large language models (LLMs).

pmc-11488193.description: Clinical Vignette:A 23-year-old woman with pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration (PKAN) presented with medication-refractory generalized dystonia and an associated gait impairment.Clinical Dilemma:Bilateral globus pallidus internus (GPi) deep brain stimulation (DBS) can be an effective treatment for dystonia. pmc-12609025.creator: Rafael Cabral, Ricardo Santos, José A. F. O. Correia, Diogo Ribeiro
pmc-12609025.description: The automated inspection of civil infrastructure with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is hampered by the challenge of accurately segmenting multi-damage in high-resolution imagery. pmc-13531260.title: Revisiting Enzyme Replacement Therapy for Aspartylglucosaminuria: Truncated Phosphotransferase Enhances Mannose‐6‐Phosphorylation and Cellular Uptake of Aspartylglucosaminidase
pmc-13531260.creator: Antje Banning, Lidia Reznikova, Adla Murad, Ritva Tikkanen
pmc-13531260.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aspartylglucosaminuria (AGU) is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by a deficiency of aspartylglucosaminidase (AGA), a hydrolase involved in the degradation of N‐glycosylated proteins. Currently, no approved therapies are available for AGU. Development of enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) for AGU has been hampered by the complex proteolytic processing and activation of the AGA enzyme that involves dimerization and cleavage into two subunits. Targeting of AGA into lysosomes is mainly accomplished by a mannose‐6‐phosphate receptor‐mediated pathway, and both AGA subunits contain phosphorylated N‐glycans.

pmc-13556818.title: 256. Improving working memory in mice using pro-cognitive drugs in the trial unique non-matched to location task
pmc-13556818.creator: B van der Veen, T M Ionescu, S Deiana, W Nissen, C T Wotjak, J du Hoffmann
pmc-13556818.description: BackgroundThe trial unique non-matched to location (TUNL) task is a touchscreen-based assay of working memory in rodents. While pharmacological impairment is widely used in rats, pharmacological enhancement of performance in rats or mice has not been demonstrated in literature.Aims & ObjectivesWe employed a recently optimized mouse version of the TUNL task to test compounds modulating glutamatergic and cholinergic signaling.
